Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 99, verses 1–2:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Zalzalah (The Earthquake)

Ibn Kathir said: it is Meccan. Al-Suyuti preferred that it is Medinan. Its verses number eight.

al-Tirmidhi narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Idha zulzilat' (Surah 99) equals half of the Qur'an. 'Qul huwa Allahu ahad' (Surah 112) equals one third of the Qur'an. And 'Qul ya ayyuha al-kafirun' (Surah 109) equals one quarter of the Qur'an.'"

. The secret of that will come in the tafsir of Surah al-Kafirun and al-Ikhlas, God willing.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[1–2] ﴿When the earth is shaken with its (final) quaking﴾ ﴿and the earth brings forth its burdens﴾ [al-Zalzalah: 2]

﴿When the earth is shaken with its (final) quaking﴾ means: that severe quaking and terrible trembling befall it. The idafa (construct) here is for emphasis (tafkhim) or specification (ikhtisas), meaning the particular quaking belonging to it, which is the shaking beyond which there is no further limit. The first (emphasis) is closer, in light of the verse: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing﴾ [al-Hajj: 1]. It was also read as zalzala with a fatha on the zay, and it has been said: both are verbal nouns (masadir). It was also said: the fatha form is a noun (ism) and the kasra form is a verbal noun (masdar), and this is the well-known view.

﴿and the earth brings forth its burdens﴾ [al-Zalzalah: 2] means: it casts out what is in its interior of treasures, hoards, the dead, and other things, due to the severity of the quaking and the splitting of its surface. Like His saying: ﴿And when the earth is stretched out﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 3] ﴿and it casts out what is within it and empties itself﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 4]. The word athqal is the plural of thaql, with fatha on both letters, which is the traveler's baggage and every precious, guarded thing. This is used metaphorically. It is also permissible that it be with kasra then sukun, meaning the burden of the belly (pregnancy), also as a figure of speech, since a load is called thiql, as in His saying: ﴿So when she became heavy﴾ [al-A'raf: 189]. This was said by al-Sharif al-Murtada in (al-Durar).

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[3–8] ﴿And man will say, "What is wrong with it?"﴾ ﴿On that Day it will report its news﴾ [Az-Zalzalah: 4] ﴿because your Lord has inspired it﴾ [Az-Zalzalah: 5] (p-6233) ﴿On that Day mankind will depart in scattered groups to be shown their deeds﴾ [Az-Zalzalah: 6] ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it﴾ [Az-Zalzalah: 7] ﴿and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾ [Az-Zalzalah: 8]

﴿And man will say, "What is wrong with it?"﴾ That is: whoever among mankind witnesses this earthquake, which surprises and astonishes him and the like of which he has never known, will say: "What is wrong with this earth, that it shakes with this terrible shaking and that what is within it of buried burdens is thrown out?!"

﴿On that Day﴾ [Az-Zalzalah: 4] is a substitute (badal) for ﴿idha﴾ (when), meaning: at that time. ﴿It will report its news﴾ [Az-Zalzalah: 4] means: the earth will make clear, through the tongue of its state, what its quaking and the bringing out of its burdens are for. It thus gives clear indication of this, which is the announcement of the end of the first creation and the appearance of another creation. So "reporting" (tahdith) is a metaphor (isti'arah) or a general metonymy (majaz mursal) in its indication.

Abu Muslim said: That is, on that Day the recompense for each person's deeds will become clear to everyone. So it is as if it had reported this, as when you say: "The house tells us that it was once inhabited." Likewise, the overturning of the earth by the quake reports that the world has come to an end and that the Hereafter has arrived.

﴿Because your Lord has inspired it﴾ [Az-Zalzalah: 5] The ba' (because) is causal (sababiyyah), and it is connected to "reports" (tuhaddith): it reports because of your Lord's inspiring it and His command to it to report. Inspiration (iya') is a metaphor or general metonymy, intended for its necessary consequence, which is the bringing about of what indicates its ruin.

Al-Qashani said: That is, He pointed to it and commanded it to be agitated, to be ruined, and to bring out its burdens, meaning the creative command (al-amr al-takwini), which is the connection of divine power to what is its effect.

﴿On that Day mankind will depart in scattered groups﴾ [Az-Zalzalah: 6] That is: they will turn away from their resting places toward the place of their reckoning and recompense, dispersed, some blessed and some wretched. ﴿to be shown their deeds﴾ [Az-Zalzalah: 6] That is: so that God may show them the recompense of their deeds.

﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it﴾ [Az-Zalzalah: 7] That is: whoever did in this world the weight of an atom of good will see its reward there. The "dharrah" (atom) is a tiny ant, and it is a proverb for smallness. It has also been said that the dharrah is the mote that is seen in sunlight when it enters through a window.

﴿and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾ [Az-Zalzalah: 8] That is: whoever had done in this world the weight of an atom of evil will see its recompense there.

(p-6234) Remarks:

First: The word "man" (man) indicates that the recompense, in both its kinds, covers the believer and others.

The Imam (al-Razi) said: That is, whoever does even the least and smallest good deed will see it and find its reward; there is no difference in this between the believer and the disbeliever. The only point is that the good deeds of disbelieving deniers do not reach the point of rescuing them from the punishment of disbelief, so they abide in wretchedness because of it. The verses that speak of the nullification of the disbelievers' deeds and that they do not benefit them mean what we have mentioned: that one deed of theirs does not save them from the punishment of disbelief, even if it lightens for them some of the punishment that awaited them for their remaining evil deeds. As for the punishment of disbelief itself, nothing of it is lightened for them. How could it not be, when God, exalted is His majesty, says: ﴿And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be wronged in anything; and even if it is the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it. And sufficient are We as reckoners﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 47]

His words ﴿so no soul will be wronged in anything﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 47] are the clearest statement that the disbeliever and the believer are equal in this, and that each will be fully paid his recompense on the Day of Resurrection. It has been reported that "Hatim is lightened for him because of his generosity," and that "Abu Lahab is lightened for him because of his joy at the birth of the Prophet (ﷺ)." As for what some have transmitted of a consensus (ijma') that the disbeliever gains no benefit in the Hereafter from any good deed and that no evil deed of his is lightened, it has no basis. Many of the leading scholars of the early generations (al-salaf), may God be pleased with them, have held what we have said. Moreover, the word "consensus" (al-ijma') is often used by the ignorant and foolish as an instrument for killing the spirit of religion and as a stone they stuff into the mouths of those who speak. They do not understand any meaning of the consensus that constitutes proof, and how wretched is what they do. End.

Al-Shihab had preceded him in his glosses on al-Qadi (Hashiyat al-Shihab), where he debated the author of (al-Maqasid) regarding his claim of consensus on the nullification of the deeds of the disbelievers. His words are: How can consensus be claimed for total nullification, when it contradicts what is stated explicitly in the verse? What appears to the mind, after investigating the secrets of the records, is that the disbelievers are punished for disbelief according to its degrees. The punishment of Abu Talib is not like the punishment of Abu Jahl, nor the punishment of the deniers of the attributes (al-mu'attilah) like the punishment of the People of the Book, as wisdom and divine justice require. End.

Second: In (al-Iklil), it is said: These two verses contain encouragement toward little and much good, and warning against little and much evil. Abd al-Razzaq reported from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: This verse is the most comprehensive verse in the Qur'an in judgment. In another wording: "the most all-encompassing."

"The Messenger of God (ﷺ) named this verse 'the comprehensive unique one' when he was asked about the zakah on donkeys, and he said: 'God has not revealed anything concerning them except this comprehensive unique verse.'"

He said: "That is enough for me. I do not mind not hearing anything other than it." Al-Nasa'i also narrated it in his Tafsir.
